questions.prompt: A model has a window of 1,000 tokens. The input is 800 tokens, and the reply may be up to 300 tokens. What happens?
options: It fits, because the input alone is less than 1,000
It does not fit, because 800 + 300 = 1,100 is more than 1,000
It fits, because the reply does not count
The model reads the first 1,000 tokens and ignores the rest
questions.explanation: The input and the reply share the window. 800 + 300 = 1,100 tokens, which is more than 1,000, so the request is too large.

questions.prompt: In the desk picture, why is the desk empty again for each request?
options: The desk is too small to hold anything
The hosted model deletes files from your computer
The model keeps nothing between requests, so the program puts everything back each time
The context window grows after each request
questions.explanation: Unlike a person, the model remembers no earlier request. The program decides what goes into the window every time it sends a request.

questions.prompt: Why can an agent fill a window of 1,048,576 tokens?
options: Each file it reads and each result it receives stays in the requests it sends after that
The window shrinks by half after every request
Each request can hold only one file
The window counts letters, not tokens
questions.explanation: An agent working for a long time keeps adding file contents and results to what it sends. Each addition stays, so the total grows until it reaches the window.
